title: Bechet visits the Stuyvesant
summary: Russell recalls Bechet attending the Stuyvesant in January 1946 and Bunk playing his best toward him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: I was going to say, one night, uh, Sidney, uh, Boucher came in, uh, that was 19, uh, the, uh, January of 1946. It had been almost a year since they'd been in Boston together, but they hadn't forgotten any of it. And, but Sidney came up to the Stuyvesant to hear him one night and sat at the table. And Bunk really perked up then and really played about the best of any time. I think I heard him at the Stuyvesant, possibly. One of the best nights he ever had. And he kept the horn pointed right at Sidney then too, most of the night. Yeah. Showing how he could blow. He really could. Sidney, he kept saying, well, I know he can blow. I always didn't say Bunk could play good and nobody was trying to give him any argument. Yeah. Sidney, I don't think it hurt him play that way probably since he was a kid, you know. Certainly not in Boston. Yeah.
